newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB affiliates' bankruptcy filing accepted.
newsitem.headline: NCB affiliates' bankruptcy filing accepted.

text.p: A bankruptcy filing by three financial firms affiliated with Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) has been accepted, Tokyo District Court said on Monday.
A court spokesman did not give further details.
NCB, a troubled long-term credit bank, said on April 1 that its three non-bank financial affiliates had filed for bankruptcy at the court as part of a restructuring.
Credit research institute Teikoku Databank has said the affiliates, which are non-bank financial institutions, have debts totalling 2.025 trillion yen.

Banking industry sources said many big Japanese banks are expected to soon revise their earnings forecasts for the year that ended on March 31 as they will dispose of problem loans provided to the three NCB affilites.
Last Friday, Daiwa Bank Ltd slashed its parent current profit forecast for 1996/97 partly because of making loan loss provisions against the three NCB affiliates.
